newsitem.title: USA: Carey says UPS deal will add 10,000 full-time jobs.
newsitem.headline: Carey says UPS deal will add 10,000 full-time jobs.

text.p: Teamster President Ron Carey said on Tuesday 10,000 new full-time jobs would be created over the five-year term covered in a newly negotiated contract with the United Parcel Service.

"We won in this agreement 10,000 new full-time jobs by combining existing low-wage, part-time positions," Carey said, adding that figure was in addition to jobs created by company growth or attrition.

Carey said the UPS pension plan would remain in a multi-group scheme and that the Teamsters "won very large pension increases -- the same or better increases the company already said it would provide."
In negotiations, UPS had been pushing for a company-controlled pension plan.

"Our members also won substantial wage increases including extra increases for part-timers," Carey said. A part-time worker who currently earns $11 per hour, under this new deal, would make more than $15 per hour by the end of the five-year contract period, he said.
Full-time workers would receive wage increases of $3.10 per hour while part-time workers would get an additional $1.00 per hour, the Teamsters union said in a statement.

"This agreement replaces subcontractors with UPS workers so as UPS grows, so do jobs grow. We won safety protection for our members who handle heavy packages," Carey told a news conference shortly after a formal announcement by Labor Secretary Alexis Herman that UPS had reached a tentative contract deal with the striking Teamsters .
Carey said if UPS wants to raise the package weight limit, it must first negotiate the change with the union.
"In virtually every area, this agreement is much, much better than the last offer before the strike," Carey said.

When asked if the Teamsters had made any concessions in the negotiations, Carey said he would have preferred a shorter contract period than the five-year agreement currently pending approval. The Teamsters last contract was a four-year deal.
The Teamsters said its members may return to work at the parcel carrier as early as Wednesday.
